SCI-FRUIT v0.1 r0.2 — TARGETED STAGE B
NORMATIVE-CORE, RESPONSE-CONDITIONING, NOI-BOUNDARY,
PRODUCT-LIFECYCLE, AND ENGINEERING-CONFORMANCE DIRECTIVE

The SCI-FRUIT r0.1 conditional scientific architecture is accepted as the
basis for one targeted Stage B revision.

Do not perform another broad FRUIT derivation.

Preserve:

- the separation among program-order authority, conditional-composition
  authority, and numerical-method authority;
- no approved numerical FRUIT method or route;
- FRUIT-FEEDBACK-METHOD v0.1 as a required-record family;
- method-specific FRUIT-FEEDBACK-METHOD/<method-name>@<revision> identities;
- exact candidate, accepted, and applied model roles and spaces;
- the applied model as the removal and rejoin operand;
- exact additive/reference/gauge/null-space compatibility;
- rho_k = y_k^in - Pi_k(m_k^applied);
- z_k = F_k(rho_k) + B_k(m_k^applied);
- the fixed-linear hierarchy and D_k only under complete linearity;
- immutable original measured-parent ancestry;
- no default iteration-input recurrence;
- distinct method, state, iteration, application, branch, and lineage identity;
- the seven operation/state categories;
- all eight support and influence roles;
- residual-and-model, residual-only, model-only, and unavailable occurrence
  classes;
- model_or_prior_supported as mode-origin state rather than measured support;
- no acquired exposure or independent observation from iteration or rejoin;
- the seven response-query scopes, subject to the conditioning repair below;
- the complete four-term parent/applied-model covariance;
- separate fixed-state, dependent-successor, and per-realization-relearned NOI
  methods;
- continuation, restart, convergence, resource limit, terminal selection, and
  consumer fitness as distinct claims;
- the nine terminal-selection fields;
- local completion separate from downstream Pointing, OOF, source, catalog, or
  production fitness;
- SCI-FRUIT-PRED-001 through PRED-020;
- every current nonclaim.

Do not inspect implementation, configuration, schemas, defaults, tests, audits,
repairs, validation products, reductions, accepted runs, performance evidence,
production material, Unity material, adjacent-package implementation, web
sources, or undocumented practice.

Preserve existing requirement, assumption, and prediction identities where
their scientific obligation is unchanged. Append new IDs only for genuinely
new independent obligations.

======================================================================
1. CREATE ONE EXACT SHARED NORMATIVE SCIENTIFIC CORE
======================================================================

Create a canonical artifact:

    SCI-FRUIT-NORMATIVE-CORE v0.1/r0.2.

The core shall be the sole normative scientific source.

It shall contain exact, stable modules or sections for:

- notation and typed spaces;
- definitions and ownership;
- equations;
- assumptions;
- product roles;
- lifecycle and state identities;
- support and information origin;
- response families;
- uncertainty families;
- exact normative requirements;
- falsifiable predictions;
- typed unavailability and edge behavior.

Convert the current 24 requirement crosswalk rows into exact normative
requirements:

    SCI-FRUIT-REQ-001 through SCI-FRUIT-REQ-024.

Each shall contain its own complete authoritative statement with normative
force. A crosswalk summary or an engineering interpretation shall not be the
only location of the requirement.

Retain:

    SCI-FRUIT-ASM-001 through SCI-FRUIT-ASM-006

and:

    SCI-FRUIT-PRED-001 through SCI-FRUIT-PRED-020.

The rationale and ECS shall both import or cite the identical core by exact
identity and SHA-256. Neither view may author broader science.

======================================================================
2. PRODUCE A REAL ENGINEERING CONFORMANCE SPECIFICATION
======================================================================

The current engineering PDF substantially reproduces the scientist document in
another order. Replace it with a prospective implementation-facing evidence
procedure.

Define one exact conformance candidate tuple containing at least:

- implementation/source identity;
- build and runtime/environment identity;
- SCI-FRUIT core identity and digest;
- method-specific FRUIT-FEEDBACK-METHOD identity and digest;
- exact parent route and generation;
- candidate/accepted/applied model generations;
- resolved operation graph and state generations;
- iteration/branch/application identity;
- output product generation;
- evidence generation.

Define one requirement-level evidence record containing:

- requirement ID;
- candidate identity;
- exact observable;
- immutable fixture;
- independent oracle or expected-value construction;
- preregistered comparison;
- result;
- artifacts;
- reviewer and date;
- deviation/failure disposition.

Use one exact engineering result vocabulary, for example:

    pass
    fail
    not_assessed
    not_applicable

with any dependency-blocked result recorded explicitly and never counted as
pass.

A finite numerical payload, successful process exit, familiar filename, or
shared array shape is not evidence of conformance.

The ECS shall define prospective evidence procedures for:

- exact parent and method binding;
- accepted-to-applied model transformation;
- operation order, bypass locations, and application counts;
- additive/reference/gauge compatibility;
- support and information-origin propagation;
- fail-closed missing or incompatible inputs;
- limiting-case equations;
- state and generation identity;
- continuation replay;
- restart and retry behavior;
- response queries;
- covariance propagation;
- NOI parity;
- terminal selection;
- publication and immutable parentage.

Where no numerical method is approved, the numerical conformance result is
not_assessed or blocked by the exact named dependency. It is never pass by
virtue of the generic contract.

Include:

- requirement-to-evidence index;
- prediction-to-fixture index;
- source/build/core parity procedure;
- blank conformance-result template;
- explicit distinction among engineering conformance, response/representation
  fidelity, uncertainty coverage, observational validation, performance,
  readiness, and production authorization.

======================================================================
3. SEPARATE FIXED NUMERICAL RESPONSE FROM FIXED-RULE RECOMPUTATION
======================================================================

The r0.1 wording says RF-01/RF-02 hold declared maps and state fixed, but later
requires prescribed coefficients to be recomputed under a perturbed operand.

Make the response conditioning exact.

Preferred disposition:

A. RF-01 fixed one-step measured-input response

Hold fixed:

- the realized numerical Pi_k, F_k, and B_k maps;
- every numerical coefficient;
- the applied model;
- support;
- reference/gauge/null-space state;
- branch;
- all other consequential state.

Perturb only y_k^in.

B. RF-02 fixed one-step applied-model response

Hold fixed:

- the realized numerical Pi_k, F_k, and B_k maps;
- every numerical coefficient;
- the measured input;
- support;
- reference/gauge/null-space state;
- branch;
- all other consequential state.

Perturb only m_k^applied.

C. RF-03 one-iteration full-procedure response

Rerun every coefficient, model, support, selection, or state realization that
the unchanged iteration rule prescribes, while holding prior S_k and the
upstream producer procedure/state fixed.

A fixed-structure/recomputed-coefficient procedure may claim RF-01/RF-02 only
when an exact proof establishes that its complete induced numerical input-output
map is one fixed operator on the declared domain and support.

Otherwise its prescribed recomputation belongs to RF-03 or another separately
typed procedure response.

Freezing coefficient values when the declared procedure recomputes them changes
the query. Recomputing coefficients when the declared response freezes them
also changes the query.

Update RF-01, RF-02, RF-03, REQ-012/013, PRED-006/009/010, the PTC
application crosswalk, and the ECS response evidence.

======================================================================
4. ADD THE GENERAL DIFFERENTIABLE FIXED-STATE RESPONSE
======================================================================

When Pi_k, F_k, and B_k are differentiable on exact compatible tangent spaces,
with every declared state and support fixed, define:

    J_(z<-y,k)^fixed
      =
      D F_k evaluated at rho_k;

    J_(z<-m,k)^fixed
      =
      D B_k evaluated at m_k^applied
      -
      [D F_k evaluated at rho_k]
      o
      [D Pi_k evaluated at m_k^applied].

Bind:

- tangent/reference/gauge spaces;
- perturbation units and basis;
- baseline;
- support;
- codomain;
- derivative convention;
- conditioning.

Under complete fixed linearity these reduce to:

    J_(z<-y,k)^fixed = A_k

    J_(z<-m,k)^fixed = D_k.

If differentiability, branch comparability, support comparability, or gauge
compatibility fails, the requested response is unavailable or a separately
typed finite-difference/state-transition object.

Do not substitute the fixed derivative for RF-03, RF-04, RF-05, RF-06, or
RF-07.

======================================================================
5. REPAIR THE FIXED-STATE NOI ACTION AND CENTERING
======================================================================

Distinguish a complete science-product map from a centered perturbation map.

For a full parent realization Y_b with fixed applied model:

    Z_b
      =
      A_k Y_b
      +
      D_k m_k^applied

under the complete fixed-linear premises.

Its center is:

    E[Z_b]
      =
      A_k E[Y_b]
      +
      D_k m_k^applied.

For a centered perturbation delta Y_b with fixed model and state:

    delta Z_b
      =
      A_k delta Y_b.

The deterministic model-path term shall not be added to every zero-centered
perturbation realization.

Every FRUIT-to-NOI boundary shall state whether an ensemble member represents:

- a full parent realization;
- a centered perturbation;
- a residual;
- a complete FRUIT output;
- or another exact quantity.

For the current ordinary SCI-NOI ensemble whose admitted target mean is zero
and whose initial uncertainty product is an uncentered second moment about
that known zero, use the compatible centered-perturbation action unless a
separately approved nonzero-center ensemble/estimator exists.

Do not apply the complete affine FRUIT science-product map to zero-centered
members and then call the uncentered second moment a zero-centered uncertainty.

A full-affine-member route requires:

- exact member center;
- transformed center;
- exact centering or second-moment convention;
- response and support parity;
- compatible uncertainty estimator;
- separately bound method identity.

Per-realization relearning of the model, support, cleaner, coefficients,
stopping, or terminal selector remains a separate method and ensemble.

Update REQ-016, PRED-011/018, the uncertainty section, method-record template,
and FLT/NOI boundary language.

======================================================================
6. KEEP STOCHASTIC CONDITIONING PRE-OUTCOME
======================================================================

Replace any ambiguous use of Omega_k^FRUIT with one exact pre-outcome
conditioning object, provisionally:

    Omega_(k,pre)^FRUIT.

It may bind:

- parent role, population, method, and generation;
- exact stochastic-law identity;
- operators and operator rules;
- support and domains;
- reference/gauge/null-space coordinates;
- resolved state;
- grouping;
- fixed selection rules;
- assumptions.

It shall not condition a stochastic target on:

- the realized numerical parent values;
- the realized applied-model values when model variance is being estimated;
- successful execution;
- a selected favorable branch;
- convergence;
- terminal selection;
- publication;
- censoring;
- or a draw-dependent domain.

If the realized applied model is deliberately conditioned fixed, state that
target explicitly. Its covariance and parent-model cross terms then vanish only
inside that narrower conditional target, and model-learning variation remains
omitted.

If the applied model is random, retain its covariance and both parent-model
cross terms.

Do not call these two uncertainty targets equivalent.

======================================================================
7. TYPE MODEL-ERROR TRANSFER BEFORE CLAIMING BIAS
======================================================================

Retain the exact fixed-linear relation:

    Delta z_k^model
      =
      D_k delta m_k^applied.

Name this primary object:

    model_error_transfer

or:

    model_induced_output_shift.

It is not automatically bias.

Define a model-induced bias only when the method supplies:

- one exact target estimand;
- one reference or truth model;
- a declared model-error random variable;
- a probability law;
- exact conditioning.

Then:

    b_(z,k)^model
      =
      E[D_k delta m_k^applied | Omega_(k,pre)^FRUIT].

If no target/reference model or expectation authority exists, bias is
unavailable while the declared output shift or sensitivity may remain
available.

Accepted-model error must be transformed through the exact
accepted-to-applied relation before it can enter this equation.

Update Equation 4 interpretation, PRED-005, uncertainty roles, and product
vocabulary.

======================================================================
8. SEPARATE MODEL-STAGE UNCERTAINTY ROLES
======================================================================

Do not use one undifferentiated
“candidate/accepted/applied model covariance” state.

Keep separately addressable:

- candidate-model/prior uncertainty;
- candidate-selection uncertainty;
- accepted-model covariance;
- acceptance-to-application transformation uncertainty;
- applied-model covariance;
- measured-parent/applied-model cross covariance;
- external-prior uncertainty;
- model-mismatch and bias.

An accepted-model covariance becomes an applied-model covariance only through
the exact transformation and dependence rules.

Storage in one container is allowed only when every role, domain, unit,
conditioning, availability, cause, generation, and omitted term remains
lossless.

======================================================================
9. DEFINE STABLE PRODUCT ROLES AND AN ORDERED PRODUCER LIFECYCLE
======================================================================

Create exact product identities for at least:

    SCI-FRUIT/ITERATION-RESULT
    SCI-FRUIT/ITERATION-BUNDLE
    SCI-FRUIT/SUCCESSOR-STATE
    SCI-FRUIT/CONTINUATION-STATE
    SCI-FRUIT/PATH-SUPPORT
    SCI-FRUIT/INFORMATION-ORIGIN
    SCI-FRUIT/RESPONSE/<RF-role>
    SCI-FRUIT/UNCERTAINTY/<role>
    SCI-FRUIT/TERMINAL-SELECTION
    SCI-FRUIT/TERMINAL-PRODUCT.

Use an ordered local lifecycle such as:

    not_requested
    requested
    effective
    unavailable
    application_scope_resolved
    applied
    iteration_realized
    complete_iteration_candidate
    completion_decided
    completed_iteration
    published
    failed
    not_produced
    superseded.

Define:

- applied:
    the exact resolved operation was invoked;

- iteration_realized:
    immutable numerical path values and execution-outcome records exist;

- complete_iteration_candidate:
    every universal and method-required role has an exact value or a
    core/method-permitted typed status;

- completion_decided:
    the FRUIT-owned local completion decision exists;

- completed_iteration:
    the candidate satisfies the exact local completion rule;

- published:
    the immutable completed product is exposed under its product role.

Do not fabricate later lifecycle records after an earlier unavailable or failed
terminal state. Preserve every stage actually reached.

A terminal selection consumes one or more completed iterations and creates a
separate immutable selector record. It never mutates a selected iteration.

A downstream Pointing, OOF, source, catalog, or production-use decision is a
separate child decision and is not required for base local completion.

======================================================================
10. REQUIRE TERMINAL-CANDIDATE COMPARABILITY
======================================================================

A terminal-selection population shall contain scientifically comparable
candidates.

Every candidate shall share, or be mapped by one exact selector-owned
transformation into, a common:

- scientific quantity and role;
- unit and scale;
- frame/grid/domain;
- additive reference/gauge;
- response meaning;
- support comparison domain;
- method and generation relation;
- uncertainty/metric meaning.

Equal array shape or a common scalar diagnostic is not comparability.

If the selector compares different methods, routes, groupings, gauges,
generations, or support domains, the exact conversion and comparison rule is
part of the terminal-selection method identity.

The selector shall retain:

- every candidate and inclusion/exclusion state;
- every conversion;
- ties;
- unavailable comparisons;
- causes;
- selected-terminal response;
- selected-terminal uncertainty.

No final, latest, lowest-residual, or visually favorable iteration is selected
by default.

======================================================================
11. KEEP LOCAL COMPLETION INDEPENDENT OF DOWNSTREAM USE
======================================================================

FRUIT owns:

- local iteration completeness;
- recurrence;
- convergence and stopping;
- terminal selection;
- local product publication.

Downstream owners retain:

- Pointing admission;
- OOF admission;
- source-inference admission;
- catalog admission;
- production fitness.

SCI-VAL may bind and evaluate an exact owner-approved use policy. It does not
run FRUIT, advance the recurrence, select the model, or choose the terminal
iteration.

An absent, unrequested, unavailable, incomplete, failed, or not-produced
downstream decision shall not erase an otherwise complete FRUIT iteration or
terminal product.

Later downstream decisions reference the immutable FRUIT parent and do not
mutate it or create a new FRUIT iteration generation.

======================================================================
12. SEPARATE THE THREE DOCUMENT ROLES
======================================================================

Produce three canonical views.

A. SCI-FRUIT-NORMATIVE-CORE

Contains the exact science, including all requirements, assumptions,
predictions, product roles, and lifecycle states.

B. SCI-FRUIT-SCIENTIFIC-RATIONALE

Retain:

- scientific motivation;
- conditional composition;
- three model roles;
- support and information origin;
- key response and covariance equations;
- iteration/continuation/terminal interpretation;
- present unavailability and claim ceilings.

Do not reproduce the complete requirement crosswalk, full method-record
template, complete prediction register, or engineering evidence procedure.

Soft target: 8–10 readable pages.

C. SCI-FRUIT-ENGINEERING-CONFORMANCE

Contain only:

- conformance object;
- evidence model;
- record contracts;
- requirement-to-evidence index;
- prediction-to-fixture index;
- comparison and numerical-policy requirements;
- response/covariance/NOI evidence procedures;
- continuation and terminal-selection tests;
- source/build/parity controls;
- result and nonclaim rules.

Do not reproduce the complete scientific rationale.

Soft target: 10–14 readable pages.

The normative core may be approximately 16–20 pages. Page targets are editorial
guides, not permission to reduce typography or remove science.

Optional full archival views may append the core, but the concise rationale and
ECS shall remain the canonical reading surfaces.

14. REQUIRED PREDICTION REPAIRS
======================================================================

Preserve SCI-FRUIT-PRED-001 through PRED-020.

Amend existing predictions where the same obligation is being clarified.

Add new prediction IDs only if needed for genuinely independent obligations.

Ensure explicit fixtures or deductions cover:

- fixed numerical operator versus prescribed coefficient recomputation;
- general differentiable response reducing to A_k and D_k under complete
  linearity;
- a zero-centered NOI perturbation receiving A_k delta y and not a deterministic
  rejoin term;
- a full affine ensemble requiring its exact transformed center;
- pre-outcome conditioning versus conditioning on a realized model;
- model-induced output shift versus bias;
- accepted-to-applied uncertainty transformation;
- terminal candidate comparability;
- lifecycle early stop without fabricated later records;
- downstream-use failure without mutation of local FRUIT completion.
